description: Baseline circuit without sizing (U8k): unit devices (m = 1), load R1 = R2 = 8 kOhm, tail bias vb = 1 V, and input 1.4 GHz (tt, 27 C, VDD = 1 V, g_1.4G_8k_1.0_10f_m1). All eight outputs divide to 700.0 MHz, with Q1 swinging from 0.749 V to 0.978 V.

Selection of R: load resistance was swept from 5 to 12 kOhm (12 runs) at vb = 0.8 V and 1 V. Division fails up to 6 kOhm and succeeds from 7 kOhm at vb = 1 V; at vb = 0.8 V it fails up to 7 kOhm and divides from 8 kOhm. The value R = 8 kOhm at vb = 1 V was selected as the minimum round value dividing at both biases.

Failure of paper sizing: direct implementation of the paper rule (m = 1, R1 = R2 = Ron/2 = 1.15 kOhm, Ron = 2.3 kOhm) fails to divide at 1.4 GHz. Output Q1 oscillates at 2799.8 MHz (2.0 x f_in) with only 15.3 mV swing (Figure 9). Supply power is 0.165 mW; delay, PDP, and phase error are undefined.

Mechanism: the pull-down path comprises three stacked devices (M1, M5, M7) with effective resistance 3 Ron = 6.90 kOhm for m = 1. Regeneration requires R1 >= 1.1 x 3 Ron = 7.59 kOhm, consistent with simulated bounds of 6-7 kOhm at vb = 1 V and 7-8 kOhm at vb = 0.8 V.

devices.role: tail current source, gate at vb = 1 V

description: Sized divider (design D): device multiplier m = 4, load R1 = R2 = 3 kOhm, and input 1.4 GHz. The pull-down stack resistance is 3 Ron/m = 1.72 kOhm, requiring load resistance of 1.90 kOhm (tolerance band 1.88 to 2.25 kOhm). Load R = 3 kOhm provides adequate margin. The same sizing rule applies to design B at 6 GHz (m = 4, R1 = R2 = 2 kOhm). Transistor M7 operates in triode, with transient drain voltage remaining below Vdsat.

Comparison with baseline (Table 3): sizing cuts delay from 62.21 ps (U8k) to 25.99 ps (D) (2.39x) and increases swing from 0.2289 V to 0.4344 V. Power rises from 0.1375 mW to 0.5413 mW (3.94x), PDP from 8.557 fJ to 14.067 fJ (1.64x), and phase-step error from 26.42 deg to 38.46 deg at 1.4 GHz.

theory: Topology. The divider consists of four differential D-latches in a ring with alternating cross-connections (Q1b-D2, Q2-D3, Q3b-D4, Q4-D1b) and inverted clocks on latches 2 and 3 (Kuo et al.). Each latch contains sampling pair M1-M2, clock switches M5-M6, regenerative hold pair M3-M4, tail transistor M7, and loads R1-R2. Sampling occurs when CK is high, and regeneration occurs when CK is low, producing eight phases at half the input frequency.

Elmore delay model. Latch propagation delay is modeled as t_pd = (8C)(R/2) = 4RC, where each output carries effective capacitance 8C and load R/2 = R1. Division requires T_CK/2 > 2 Td. For load capacitance C_L = 10 fF, the parasitic-free lower bound is Td >= R1 C_L, yielding 30 ps for design D (R1 = 3 kOhm) and 20 ps for design B (R1 = 2 kOhm). At 1.4 GHz (design D), 2 Td >= 60 ps satisfies T_CK/2 = 357 ps. At 6 GHz (design B), 2 Td >= 40 ps satisfies T_CK/2 = 83 ps. Design B divides up to 6 GHz and fails at 6.2 GHz (T_CK/2 = 80.6 ps). Its measured CK-to-Q1 delay of 66.10 ps is 3.3x the intrinsic lower bound (79% of T_CK/2), showing that parasitic capacitances dominate near the frequency limit.

Stack resistance and regeneration. The pull-down network forms a three-transistor stack (M1, M5, M7) with effective resistance 3 Ron/m. Latch regeneration requires gm R1 > 1, yielding R1 >= 1.1 x (3 Ron/m). With Ron = 2.3 kOhm, the unit stack is 6.90 kOhm, requiring R1 >= 7.59 kOhm. The paper load (1.15 kOhm) falls far below this threshold, preventing division. Measured thresholds for m = 1 span 6 to 7 kOhm at vb = 1 V, and 7 to 8 kOhm at vb = 0.8 V. For m = 4, the required threshold is 1.90 kOhm (band 1.88 to 2.25 kOhm); design D (R1 = 3 kOhm) provides margin, while design B (R1 = 2 kOhm) operates within the marginal band. Measured division agrees with the rule for 5 of 5 tested parameter pairs. The unit device aspect ratio W/L = 5.33 (240 nm / 45 nm) matches the reference design ratio of 5.00 (0.9 um / 180 nm).

Phase-step relationship. Outputs toggle in pairs separated by t_pair (measured between rising edges of Q2 and Q3b), yielding phase step a = 180 t_pair f_in degrees, alternating with 90 - a degrees. For design D at 1.4 GHz, t_pair = 25.95 ps gives steps of 83.46 and 6.54 deg (a = 180 x 25.95 ps x 1.4 GHz = 6.54 deg). For design B at 6 GHz, t_pair = 38.16 ps gives 48.78 and 41.22 deg (a = 41.22 deg). Baseline U8k at 1.4 GHz gives 71.42 and 18.59 deg (t_pair = 73.75 ps, a = 18.59 deg). Nominal 45 deg spacing requires T_CK = 4 t_pair: 103.8 ps (9.63 GHz) for D and 152.7 ps (6.55 GHz) for B. Phase error decreases as frequency increases toward the divider limit, matching the reference paper value (3.75 deg) only in design B at 6 GHz.

Definitions of performance metrics. Delay is the average time from each CK rising edge to the next transition on any output (25.99 ps for design D; single-edge CK-to-Q1 delay is 51.95 ps). Power is VDD times the average supply current over full cycles. PDP is power times delay (fJ). Division is valid when all eight outputs toggle at f_in/2 within 0.1 percent with peak-to-peak swing >= 0.1 V.
tool_technology: Tools and environment: Cadence Virtuoso IC615 (6.1.5), Spectre circuit simulator (MMSIM 12.1), and Assura physical verification (4.1). Process technology is Cadence GPDK045 v6.0 (45 nm generic CMOS), using standard-threshold NMOS devices (g45n1svt, 1.0 V nominal) evaluated across tt, ff, ss, fs, and sf corners.
Device sizing: unit transistors M1-M6 have W = 240 nm, L = 45 nm, and tail transistor M7 has W = 480 nm, L = 90 nm. Device multiplier m scales channel widths in parallel.

Operating conditions: nominal supply VDD = 1 V (PVT range 0.9 V to 1.1 V), nominal temperature 27 C, clock transition times 20 ps, tail bias vb = 1 V, and load capacitance 10 fF per output. Simulation dataset: "Transient Analysis `tran': time = (0 s -> 40 ns)" (12:25:58 PM, Sat Oct 31, 2026).

Virtuoso schematic parameter extraction for the design D DLATCH cell: R1 and R2 = 3 kOhm; M1-M6 w = 240n, l = 45n, m = 4; M7 w = 480n, l = 90n, m = 4. These match Table 2 and the nominal transistor dimensions.
Circuit schematics for the DLATCH and ring architecture are illustrated in Figure 1 and Figure 8.
other_info: Layout. The DLATCH cell contains 7 unit nMOS pcells (0.595 um wide) and 2 poly resistors (segW 0.8 um, segL 7.855 um, 200 ohm/sq, target 2000 ohm). Transistors M1-M6 use 2 fingers of 120 nm (240 nm, L = 45 nm); M7 uses 4 fingers of 120 nm (480 nm, L = 90 nm) for m = 1. Design D requires 4x width (m = 4) and 3 kOhm load (baseline uses 8 kOhm). DLATCH boundary is 4.875 x 20.28 um. Cell divider_core places XD1 R0, XD2 MY, XD3 MX, XD4 R180 with a 1 um gap (clock-star length 98.62 um each). The layout is placement only: it is not routed, and LVS and post-layout simulation were not run. An automatic routing run with Cadence's Chip Assembly Router completed 136 of 137 connections but produced 134 DRC errors and mismatches in LVS, so the placement layout is the one reported. Cell layouts are shown in Figure 7 (divider_core) and Figure 22 (DLATCH).

DRC verification. Assura DRC on DLATCH reports 21 errors across 3 rules (Figure 23). Rules 220 (1) and 221 (6) give 7 substrate-stamp errors from unrouted taps at device pitch 0.755 um. Rule 595 (14) gives 14 Metal1 minimum-area errors (threshold 0.02 um^2); 4 markers measure 0.06 x 0.12 um (0.0072 um^2) across x = 0.96-1.155 um, y = 1-2.02 um. Contact pins (0.2 x 0.15 um = 0.03 um^2) meet the minimum area. The unrouted layout is not DRC clean.

Schematic connectivity. Pin-by-pin comparison of the 4 DLATCH instances (XD1-XD4) against the netlist confirmed full consistency with 0 mismatches. Schematic check warnings: DLATCH 0/0, divider_core 0/0, and tb_divider 0/1.

Design B operating point. At 6 GHz (m = 4, R1 = R2 = 2 kOhm), the divider achieves 3000.0 MHz output, 0.4929 mW power, 27.94 ps delay, 13.768 fJ PDP, and 3.78 deg maximum phase error (48.78 and 41.22 deg steps). Output Q1 swings 0.135 V (0.818 V to 0.953 V), above the 0.1 V limit. Peak tail voltage reaches 66.2 mV, below Vdsat = 357.8 mV (triode, Figure 14). PVT results appear in Table 4.

DC operating points. At t = 0 (clocks low, switches off), tail current is negligible (Vgs = 1 V). For paper sizing, M7 is in triode (Vds = 56.3 nV, Ids = 35.6 pA). For design D, M7 is in triode (Vds = 54.4 nV, Ids = 137.4 pA). For design B (m = 4, vb = 1 V), M7 is in triode (Vds = 54.4 nV, Ids = 137.4 pA).

Tail transistor operating region. With Vgs = 1 V and Vth = 527.5 mV, extracted Vdsat is 357.8 mV (at t = 0, gm = 200.9 pS, gds = 2.531 mS, Vds = 54 nV). In transient operation, V(XD1.tail) spans 8.1 to 66.9 mV for design D (XD2 reaches 68.2 mV) and 8.0 to 67.1 mV for baseline U8k. Because Vds remains below Vdsat, M7 operates in triode rather than saturation (Figures 12 and 13).

Frequency sweeps. Design B (m = 4, R = 2 kOhm) was swept from 1.4 to 6.2 GHz: it divides at 1.4, 2, 3, 4, 5, 5.5, 5.8, 6 GHz and fails at 6.2 GHz. Design D (m = 4, R = 3 kOhm) was swept from 3 to 8 GHz: it divides at 3, 4, 5, 5.5 GHz and fails at 6, 6.5, 7, 8 GHz (the 1.4 GHz operating point also divides). Design E (m = 6, R = 2 kOhm) was swept from 3 to 8 GHz: it divides at 3, 4, 5, 5.5, 6, 6.5, 7 GHz and fails at 8 GHz (1.4 GHz divides at tt, 27 C, 1.0 V). Maximum phase-step error at the highest dividing frequency is 3.78 deg for B, 13.82 deg for D, and 15.24 deg for E, compared with 38.68, 30.89, and 34.32 deg at the lower frequency bounds. In all cases, phase error improves as frequency increases (Figure 16).

Parameter exploration (16 points): m = 4, R = 2.2 kOhm divides up to 6.25 GHz (5.57 deg phase-step error there); m = 4, R = 2.5 kOhm divides up to 6 GHz (11.23 deg phase-step error there) and fails at 6.25 GHz; m = 5, R = 2.2 kOhm divides up to 6.25 GHz (16.56 deg phase-step error there); m = 5, R = 2.5 kOhm divides up to 6.25 GHz (14.36 deg phase-step error there). These nominal simulations characterize the upper operating boundary near the frequency limit of design B.

Transient delay and edge times. First-edge CK-to-Q1 delays are 135.96 ps (U8k), 51.95 ps (design D), and 66.10 ps (design B). Multi-phase average delay for design D is 25.99 ps. Output Q1 rise and fall times are 134.6 ps and 102.6 ps.
Supply current. Design D average supply current is 0.54144 mA (0.541337 mA integrated from transient, matching within 0.018%). Peak current is 0.560 mA (Figure 15).

Comparison with reference literature. Reported values from Kuo et al. (TSMC 180 nm, 1.8 V, 1.4 GHz) are 2.34 mW, phase error within 3.75 deg, and core area 91.7 x 52.9 um^2. In 45 nm, design D at 1.4 GHz consumes 0.5413 mW with 38.46 deg phase error; design B reaches 3.78 deg at 6 GHz.

Figure index. Primary figures 1 to 7 cover schematics, waveforms, and layout. Figures 8 onwards provide supplementary validation: ring architecture (Figure 8), paper sizing waveforms (Figure 9), design B waveforms at 6 GHz (Figure 10), phase steps (Figure 11), tail node voltages (Figures 12, 13, and 14), supply current (Figure 15), frequency sweeps (Figure 16), PVT distributions (Figures 17, 18, and 19), testbench schematic (Figure 20), session log (Figure 21), DLATCH layout (Figure 22), DRC summary (Figure 23), and transient waveform plot for design D (Figure 24).
conclusion: Multiphase CMOS division in 45 nm was demonstrated at two operating points using the stack resistance rule. Design D at 1.4 GHz (m = 4, R = 3 kOhm) achieved 0.5413 mW, 25.99 ps delay, 14.067 fJ PDP, and 38.46 deg phase error (41 of 45 PVT corners passing). Design B at 6 GHz (m = 4, R = 2 kOhm) achieved 0.4929 mW, 27.94 ps delay, 13.768 fJ PDP, and 3.78 deg phase error (21 of 45 PVT corners passing). Design B exhibited reduced swing (0.135 V, 0.818 V to 0.953 V against the 0.1 V limit), failed at tt, 27 C, 0.9 V, and failed division at 6.2 GHz.

Baseline comparison: sizing cuts delay from 62.21 ps (U8k) to 25.99 ps (D) (2.39x) and increases swing from 0.2289 V to 0.4344 V. Power rises from 0.1375 mW to 0.5413 mW (3.94x), PDP from 8.557 fJ to 14.067 fJ (1.64x), and phase-step error from 26.42 deg to 38.46 deg at 1.4 GHz.

The paper sizing rule (m = 1, R1 = Ron/2 = 1.15 kOhm) fails to divide at 1.4 GHz because load resistance is below the regeneration threshold (7.59 kOhm). Empirical division thresholds span 7 to 8 kOhm at vb = 0.8 V, and 6 to 7 kOhm at vb = 1 V.

Operating limitations: transistor M7 operates in triode across all designs. Phase-step error at 1.4 GHz (38.46 deg) exceeds the literature value (3.75 deg); 3.78 deg was reached only at 6 GHz. All 4 PVT failures for design D occur at 125 C and 0.9 V. Design B operates near the regeneration boundary, passing 21 of 45 PVT points at 6 GHz and 27 of 45 at 1.4 GHz.

Layout implementation: placement was performed for unit-size transistors (m = 1) and placeholder resistors (2000 ohm); routing, LVS, extraction, and post-layout simulation were not performed (design D with m = 4 and R = 3 kOhm was not laid out). DLATCH DRC yields 21 errors across 3 rules (7 substrate connectivity, 14 Metal1 minimum area).
problems_faced: Compilation failure in Spectre AHDL/CMI module compilation for the gpdk045 BSIM4 model.
32-bit simulation environment compatibility with Cadence tool dependencies and compiler toolchain.
Storage space limitations during multi-corner parameter sweeps.
Failure of paper sizing (R1 = Ron/2) to divide at 1.0, 1.4, or 2.0 GHz, requiring an empirical search for load resistance.
False division detection caused by low-amplitude harmonics at 2 f_in (2.8 GHz at 1.4 GHz input) with only 13 to 20 mV swing.
Transient raw data parsing constraints during multi-signal simulation extraction.
High-temperature PVT failure at 125 C for marginal sizing designs.
Data transfer constraints within the isolated simulation environment.
Large phase-step error at 1.4 GHz (38.46 deg) compared with the reference literature value of 3.75 deg.
Layout incomplete: placement only (m = 1) without routing, yielding 21 DRC errors (7 substrate stamp, 14 Metal1 minimum area); LVS and post-layout simulation were not run.
problems_resolved: Configured host C compiler (gcc 4.4.7) and runtime libraries to support Spectre AHDL model compilation.
Extracted and validated simulation parameters systematically across nominal, corner, and sweep conditions.
Identified dividing unit-size load resistance across 12 simulations and applied the stack resistance rule to establish design D (41 of 45 PVT points passing).
Enforced strict division verification: all eight phases must operate at f_in/2 within 0.1% with peak-to-peak swing >= 0.1 V.
Verified consistency across transient output metrics and automated simulation summaries.
Characterized divider performance at two operating points: 1.4 GHz (reference comparison) and 6 GHz (minimized phase error).
Executed batch Assura physical verification on the DLATCH cell to quantify placement design rule violations.

schematic_sim.heading: Simulation driven directly from the Virtuoso schematic (OCEAN)
paragraphs: To evaluate the sized divider circuit (design D) directly from the Cadence schematic environment, the testbench schematic was simulated with Spectre at the nominal typical corner (tt, 27 C, 1.0 V supply, 1.0 V bias) with a 1.4 GHz input clock. The circuit uses load resistors R1 = R2 = 3 kOhm and transistor multiplicity m = 4. All 8 outputs divide to 700 MHz with a frequency division ratio of 2.0.

Propagation delay from the clock to the divider outputs is 26.66 ps, compared with 25.99 ps from the standalone netlist. Average supply power is 0.455 mW, compared with 0.541 mW from the standalone netlist run. The power differs by about 16 percent between the two flows. The cause is under investigation; the averaging window and the device parameters added by the Virtuoso netlister differ; the standalone value is used for the power and PDP tables.
schematic_sim.figure_ref: The testbench schematic is shown in Figure 20.
